entries.name: rootwell-hero-initial.png
entries.role: Initial square close-up, superseded by user’s isolated-asset requirement
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: detailed landmark concept art for Sparks & Machines, Haverlund's central Rootwell / root-power beacon.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved Guildhall Square painting and the PRIMARY design/style reference. Image 2 is the current in-game beacon and is ONLY a supporting reference for the functional parts and the near-isometric game viewpoint; do not copy its crude geometry, flat root or UI.
Primary request: Reframe and develop the CENTRAL POWER LANDMARK from Image 1 into a beautiful, much closer, fully painted standalone concept illustration. This is the same landmark, given architectural and mechanical specificity, not a different machine and not another whole-square image.
Composition: landscape illustration, a single large three-quarter view from slightly above at the game's orthographic heading, FULL monument including highest finial and every bottom step visible with generous margin. The monument fills most of the canvas. A small, quiet fragment of the square's cobbled paving anchors it. Behind it, only lightly suggested cream-and-timber city architecture, deliberately pale and unobtrusive; no busy market, no buildings hiding the monument. No game interface, no captions, no border.
Design invariants: Preserve the broad octagonal limestone plinth and shallow concentric steps, huge welcoming amber glass lantern containing a living illuminated ROOT emerging from the earth, dark teal/verdigris structural columns with brass collars, ribbed green copper bell-shaped roof with a smaller lantern cap and finial, oversized low brass pressure gauge facing the main approach, brass power routes entering the paving. It is a substantial city meeting-place and municipal power source, taller than a person, smaller than the surrounding guild hall.
Detail development: The root is warm living wood with branching veins and one asymmetrical main curl, visibly rooted down into a deep well throat; not a free-standing ornamental tree, fire or lightning. Several large bowed glass panes meet at credible narrow brass frames, attached securely between the lower receiver ring and roof. Show warm light through amber glass while retaining wood grain and interior silhouette. Keep glass readable and partly clear, with controlled highlights rather than opaque yellow plastic or excessive bloom.
The outer structure must make constructional sense: four substantial metal columns tied into stone sockets and copper roof ring, fastened flanges, purposeful rivets and a believable drainage lip. Brass pressure pipework connects the central chamber to the big public dial and to accessible branch valve wheels; conduits pass through the base and continue under flush grates in the cobbles, not random dangling pipes. Gauge has an ivory face, clear dark tick marks and an amber-red low-pressure arc; its needle is visibly low. Avoid elaborate tiny labels.
The stone drum has well-cut individual courses, bevelled corners and coping. On adjacent faces retain a modest roofed notice board with a few pinned papers, a comfortable timber perch, a SMALL recessed maintenance hatch with real hinges and latch, and restrained ivy/flowers growing from actual planters. These details feel civic and used without burying service access. Put wear where hands and feet touch: polished valve rims, rubbed brass, softened step edges, verdigris under seams, a few repair fasteners. No random gears or decorative machinery with no function.
Style: the approved warm, richly detailed outlined concept painting, confident fine sepia contours, readable material edges, hand-painted textures and soft sunny shadows. Painterly architectural/game production art, not a photograph, not a low-poly render, not pixel art. Warm cream limestone, teal-green patinated copper, honey brass, terracotta accents and a golden amber heart. The luminous root is the focal point but metal and masonry remain richly coloured. This should feel like a much more detailed close-up of the SAME centerpiece seen in the approved square.
Avoid: steampunk gear clutter, sci-fi reactor, holograms, neon cyan, gothic shrine, central leafy tree, floating root, arbitrary changes to the city concept, cropped finial or steps, excessive bloom, illegible text, watermark.

entries.name: rootwell-hero-refined.png
entries.role: Pressure-gauge and framing correction; supporting reference for isolated views
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the provided Rootwell beacon concept painting with ONLY these two corrections. Preserve the monument design, root, glass, copper roof, colour, sunlight, stone base, pipes, notice board, bench, service door, flowers and surrounding square.
1. The big round instrument on the front is a PRESSURE GAUGE, not a clock. Replace the Roman-numeral clock face with a clear ivory industrial pressure gauge: ONE needle; small simple Arabic numbers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 spread along an almost-three-quarter arc; a short red low-pressure sector at lower-left, warm normal range then a narrow high-end warning. The needle points into the LOW range. No Roman numerals, no clock hands, no twelve-hour clock layout. Keep the ornate teal/brass gauge housing exactly in place and at the same size.
2. Pull the camera back a little so that there is clearly visible comfortable background margin above the highest finial and below the lowest foreground grate. The WHOLE monument is in frame; nothing touches the canvas edge.
Output a polished landscape concept illustration matching the reference painting. Do not add labels, text captions or a title.

entries.name: rootwell-turnaround-initial.png
entries.role: Unselected sheet: repeated front angle and insufficient framing gutters
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / game asset concept turnaround.
Edit target: the supplied close-up Rootwell monument. Extract and DEVELOP ONLY THE MONUMENT as a consistent three-view asset sheet.
The user specifically requires NO BACKGROUND and MULTIPLE VIEWS. Use a genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha background. Absolutely no city, houses, street, sky, backdrop, coloured paper, ground plane, cast shadows outside the asset, characters, surrounding lamps, foliage belonging to the environment, UI, panel borders, text or labels. Only the asset itself and its integral planters/steps.
Composition: a wide high-resolution production concept sheet with THREE complete, separate views, side by side, aligned at the same ground baseline and the same physical scale. Leave clear transparent gutters between them and generous margin above every finial and below every step. All three entire monuments fit; never crop or overlap.
LEFT VIEW: front-right orthographic three-quarter view at the game's slightly elevated camera, showing the large front pressure gauge, notice-board/bench face on one adjacent side, and teal service-door face on the other.
MIDDLE VIEW: TRUE OPPOSITE REAR-LEFT orthographic three-quarter view, a real 180-degree turn around THE SAME OBJECT. This view reveals the rear base's purposeful relief manifold, copper riser pipes and a recessed vented service panel. The big FRONT gauge and front notice board rotate away and must not reappear pasted onto the rear. Preserve the existing adjacent service door on its correct physical face wherever visible. Do NOT mirror or invent a second front.
RIGHT VIEW: straight FRONT ORTHOGRAPHIC ELEVATION, looking horizontally at the big pressure gauge, to make the monument's overall proportions and the root/chamber/roof assembly clear. No perspective convergence.
Design lock across ALL views: SAME octagonal cream limestone plinth with shallow steps; SAME tall amber bowed-glass chamber, warm branching LIVING ROOT visibly entering the well at its bottom; SAME teal/verdigris structural uprights and warm brass collars, flanges and lower receiver ring; SAME ribbed copper dome, smaller lantern cap and finial; same number and attachment of external side lanterns. Root branches must visibly rotate consistently between front and rear rather than becoming a different plant. Same restrained ivy and actual integral flower planters, roofed noticeboard, timber perch and maintenance door. Preserve the reference's proportions, rich detail and hand-worn surfaces. Keep the root a contained source of amber magic, no leaves or sprawling tree crown.
The front instrument is an ivory PRESSURE GAUGE, with ONE needle in a red LOW range and a 0–10 arc with plain Arabic numbers. No Roman numerals or clock layout. Gauge, pipe fittings and branch valves need clear distinct silhouettes. Brass conduits from the base should end neatly as short connection stubs at the edge of the integral steps; the town's long ground routes belong to the environment and are NOT on this isolated asset sheet.
Painting: warm polished game concept art with confident fine sepia outlines, painterly hand-painted stone and metal, readable material breaks, carefully controlled golden light through transparent glass. This is the main design reference for a detailed 3D asset, so show coherent joints, glass retention, roof supports, pipe routes, hinges and service access. No low-poly simplification and no photoreal product rendering. Keep every fine detail subordinate to a clear silhouette.
Output: ONLY the three-view monument sheet on real transparency, with clean alpha edges and no background of any kind.

entries.name: rootwell-front-threequarter.png
entries.role: Selected isolated front three-quarter concept; user approved and requested v0.72
entries.prompt:
Edit the supplied Rootwell beacon painting into ONE isolated high-detail game asset concept view. Real transparent alpha background; no scenery, no sky, no city, no street or ground plane, no other props, no captions, no diagrams. Keep only the monument itself, its integral octagonal stone steps, attached planters, notice-board/perch/service fittings as appropriate for the visible side, and short brass conduit stubs ending at the steps.
Framing is critical: ONE monument centred on a tall portrait canvas, occupying at most 78 percent of the canvas height and 78 percent of its width. At least 10 percent clear transparent margin on ALL sides. Entire finial and every last step must be visible. No edge contact, no crop, no extra duplicated view. A single large painting with crisp details.
Design: same octagonal limestone base, four main teal/verdigris supports with brass collars, huge segmented bowed-glass amber chamber holding a branching living root entering the well below, ribbed copper dome, small lantern cap/finial, attached side lanterns, restrained rooted ivy and flower planters. Keep exactly the same dimensions, materials, construction and weathering as the reference. Warm, painted sepia-outline game concept art, soft consistent lighting, clearly legible gold/brass/teal/stone, controlled glow revealing the root. No leaves or big tree canopy, no steampunk gear clutter, no 3D low-poly look.
VIEW: FRONT-RIGHT orthographic three-quarter view at a modestly elevated gameplay angle. The big ivory pressure gauge is on the primary front base face, the roofed public notice board and timber perch on the front-left adjacent face, and the teal maintenance door on the front-right adjacent face. Gauge is pressure, not time: one needle low on a 0–10 arc with a red low sector, no Roman numerals. Preserve the source painting’s correct physical placement and clear pipe/valve connections.
